headline: Harvard physicist publishes 36 papers co-authored with Claude AI
body: Matthew Schwartz, a Harvard particle physicist, has published 36 research papers authored jointly with Claude, demonstrating AI's capability to contribute substantively to complex scientific work. This signals a shift in how domain experts may leverage large language models for research acceleration and knowledge synthesis. For healthcare AI specifically, this precedent raises questions about clinical validation workflows: if AI co-authorship becomes standard in peer review, how will healthcare systems validate AI-assisted diagnostic or treatment recommendations? The pattern suggests vendors and healthcare organizations should prepare for a future where AI contribution to clinical evidence generation requires new credibility frameworks distinct from traditional peer review.
